title: Demonstrators march across France over living costs and inequality

tea.why: Protesters marched to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality.
tea.want: Protesters demanded relief from high living costs and addressed growing economic inequality.
tea.changed: Oct 24: Police fired tear gas and water cannon as clashes broke out following the main demonstration.

summary: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched across France on October 24 in largely peaceful rallies to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality. The main demonstration took place in Paris, where crowds gathered on the south-eastern fringes of the capital. Organised following calls by student unions, youth groups, and other movements, the rallies drew hundreds of thousands nationwide, though official and union turnout figures differed. As night fell, the atmosphere deteriorated in Paris, Marseille, and other cities, resulting in clashes where police deployed tear gas and water cannon against groups throwing stones and projectiles. Authorities deployed 70,000 security personnel nationwide to manage the demonstrations and prevent widespread looting, following unrest during previous weekends.
response: According to the Interior Ministry, authorities deployed 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that security forces held their ground to protect city centres, while riot police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse violent groups.

crowd.text: Around 110,000 people marched on the south-eastern fringes of the capital

arrests.text: At 21 hours, nationwide, 565 people were arrested, according to the Interior Ministry

injuries.text: In the capital, five members of the security forces were injured, including three by Molotov cocktail impacts

updates.text: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched across France in rallies denouncing living costs and inequality.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported the deployment of 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide.
Clashes erupted in Paris and Marseille after dark, prompting riot police to use tear gas and water cannon.

conflicts: The Interior Ministry stated that 410,000 people participated nationwide, while unions claimed the figure was twice as high.
For the Paris protest, authorities reported 70,000 to 110,000 attendees, whereas the youth intersyndicale claimed 200,000.
